title: Infinitesimal morphisms for coherent modules on a fixed proper closed subscheme
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal such that $A$ is $I$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]. Let $f:X\to S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $n\geq0$ put $S_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/I^{n+1})$ and $X_n=X\times_S S_n$ [def-pc-base-change], and let $j_n:X_n\to X$ and $i_n:X_n\to X_{n+1}$ be the canonical closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Pullback is tensor pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]; coherent modules are as in [pqf-def-coherent]. Write $c_n:i_n^*j_{n+1}^*\cong j_n^*$ for the canonical natural comparison induced by $i_nj_{n+1}=j_n$. Let $j:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion with $Z\to S$ proper. Let $F,G$ be coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules both annihilated by the ideal sheaf $\mathcal J_Z$ of $j$, meaning $a t=0$ for all opens $V\subseteq X$, $a\in\mathcal J_Z(V)$ and $t\in F(V)$, and likewise for $G$. Then the map $w\mapsto(j_n^*w)_n$ is a bijection from $\operatorname{Hom}_X(G,F)$ to the set of families $v_n:j_n^*G\to j_n^*F$ satisfying $v_n\circ c_{n,G}=c_{n,F}\circ i_n^*v_{n+1}$ for every $n$.

source.place: Theorem 088E (theorem-grothendieck-existence), first paragraph; Lemma 0883 (lemma-fully-faithful), and Remark 088F (remark-reformulate-existence-theorem)

proof.text: X is Noetherian by finite type over Spec A, and Z is Noetherian by properness of j≫f. Coherence on X gives quasi-coherence and finite type. The annihilation theorem makes the adjunction units G→j_*j^*G and F→j_*j^*F invertible and makes the pullbacks quasi-coherent and finite type. Coherence on Z gives coherent objects GZ and FZ.

Proper completion on Z is fully faithful. Closed pushforward is fully faithful, hence so is termwise pushforward on inverse systems. Use the natural completion comparison from closedImmersion_coherentFormal_equivalence to transfer full faithfulness to the composite Coh(Z)→Modules(X)→formal systems(X). Since Coh(Z)→Modules(X) is itself fully faithful, the completion map between the two pushforward objects is bijective.

Transport the preceding bijection from j_*GZ and j_*FZ back to G and F through their invertible units. The helper map_bijective_of_isos verifies the naturality square for a functor and conjugation of Hom by isomorphisms, then proves injectivity and surjectivity.

The formal-Hom dictionary gives an equivalence e from these formal completion morphisms to the compatible restriction families, and specifies e(formalCompletionMap w)=(j_n^*w)_n. Compose its bijection with the completion bijection. Rewrite by that equation to obtain exactly the stated restriction map.
